items.q: What is an AI landing page builder?
items.a: An AI landing page builder, sometimes called an AI landing page generator or AI landing page maker, creates a complete landing page from a written description: layout, copy, form, and design. Emergent goes one step further and also generates the database the form writes to and the integrations it triggers, then publishes the page on your domain.

items.q: How does an AI landing page builder work?
items.a: You describe the campaign, the audience, and the offer. The builder interprets the brief, assembles the sections in conversion order, writes the copy, and configures the form. On Emergent the same prompt also creates the backend and connects your analytics and CRM.

items.q: What is the best AI landing page generator in 2026?
items.a: It depends on what you need to own. Roundups of the best AI landing page builders usually compare editors; the bigger question is who owns the page, the leads, and the code. If you want all three, Emergent is built for that. If you want a hosted editor with built-in traffic optimization on paid campaigns, Unbounce is the established choice. If mobile-first funnels matter most, Perspective specializes there.

items.q: Is there a free AI landing page generator?
items.a: Yes. Emergent works as a free AI landing page builder: the free tier includes monthly credits, enough to build and publish a landing page and test it with real traffic. Unbounce offers a 14-day trial, and its lowest plan caps visitors at 500 per month.

items.q: Can I publish the landing page on my own domain?
items.a: Yes. Custom domains are built into Emergent: connect a domain or subdomain and SSL is provisioned automatically, with no third-party hosting to set up. Custom domains use credits. You can also embed the page in an existing site or run it as a popup.

items.q: Does the landing page work on mobile?
items.a: Yes. Every page is generated responsive, and you can preview and adjust the phone layout before publishing.

items.q: Can I A/B test landing pages?
items.a: Yes. Ask for a second variant of the hero, the CTA, or the whole page, publish both, and compare conversion by traffic source in your analytics tool.

items.q: Can I connect the form to my CRM?
items.a: Yes. Submissions sync to HubSpot, Mailchimp, Kit (formerly ConvertKit), ActiveCampaign, Klaviyo, and any tool with a webhook or API, with campaign and source attached.

items.q: Will my landing page rank on Google?
items.a: It can. Meta title, description, and OG image are set on publish, and the page is indexable and served over SSL. Ranking still depends on the query you target and the content on the page.

items.q: Can I export the code and host it myself?
items.a: Yes. The full codebase exports to your repository. You can keep hosting on Emergent or deploy anywhere you like.

items.q: What is the difference between a landing page builder and a website builder?
items.a: A landing page targets one audience with one message and one action, usually without site navigation. A website builder produces a multi-page site with navigation and shared templates. Emergent builds both; this page covers landing pages.

items.q: How much does a landing page builder cost?
items.a: Emergent starts as a free landing page builder, with paid plans priced on usage rather than page or visitor counts. Unbounce starts at $22 per month on annual billing for 5 pages and 500 visitors, and $74 per month for unlimited pages and 20,000 visitors. Price alone does not pick the best landing page builder; check visitor caps and who owns the leads.

items.q: Can I build a landing page without having a website?
items.a: Yes. Publish the page on its own domain or subdomain. No existing site is required.

items.q: How long does it take to build a landing page with AI?
items.a: A first version is ready to preview within minutes of the prompt, since the layout, copy, and form are drafted together. Plan another fifteen to thirty minutes to refine copy, check the form end to end, and connect your domain.

items.q: What is an AI form builder?
items.a: An AI form builder, also called an AI form generator, is an online form creator that works from a written description: it picks the fields, field types, validation, and layout for you. Emergent also generates the database the form writes to, the conditional logic, and the integrations, from the same prompt.

items.q: How does an AI form builder work?
items.a: You describe what the form collects, any rules, and where the data should go. Unlike a drag and drop form builder, there is no canvas to arrange. The AI form creator picks field types, writes validation, adds branching, and produces a form you can refine by describing changes. On Emergent the submission destination is a database you own, created at the same time.

items.q: What is the best AI form builder in 2026?
items.a: It depends on what you need to own. If you want the responses in a database you control with no caps, Emergent is built for that. If you want the conversational one-question-at-a-time style and are fine with metered responses, Typeform is the established choice. If template breadth matters most, Jotform has one of the largest template libraries.

items.q: Is there a free AI form builder?
items.a: Yes. Emergent is a free online form builder to start, with monthly credits and no response cap. Typeform's free plan allows 10 responses per month and Jotform's allows 5 forms and 100 submissions per month; both stop collecting at the cap.

items.q: Which AI form builder has conditional logic?
items.a: Most AI form makers stop at generating fields. Emergent includes conditional fields, scoring, calculations, and routing on every plan. Typeform includes basic logic on every plan and advanced logic from Plus. Jotform includes conditions on all plans. Google Forms supports basic section branching.

items.q: Can the form take payments?
items.a: Yes. Add a Stripe payment step and the form collects the payment before or after the submission is saved. PayPal is also supported.

items.q: Where does the form data live?
items.a: Responses from AI forms built on Emergent land in a database table inside your project, which you can query, filter, and export. You can also sync each submission to Google Sheets, Airtable, Notion, or your CRM.

items.q: Can I connect the form to my CRM?
items.a: Yes. HubSpot, Salesforce, Mailchimp, and Klaviyo are supported directly, and any other tool through a webhook or API.

items.q: Can I embed the form on my existing website?
items.a: Yes. Use an inline embed or iframe on WordPress, Webflow, Shopify, or any site. Teams that would otherwise install a WordPress form builder plugin paste one embed instead. The form also works as a standalone page or a popup.

items.q: Is there a response limit?
items.a: No. Emergent does not meter responses. Typeform caps responses at 10 per month free and 100 on Basic; Jotform caps at 100 per month free and 1,000 on Bronze. Both stop collecting when the cap is reached.

items.q: Can I export the code?
items.a: Yes. The full codebase, including the form markup and its backend, exports to your repository, so Emergent doubles as an HTML form builder when you need raw code. Host it anywhere.

items.q: Is Emergent suitable for sensitive data like patient intake?
items.a: Emergent is SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001 certified. For regulated workflows such as HIPAA, contact sales about Enterprise terms before collecting protected health information.

items.q: What is the difference between a form builder and a survey tool?
items.a: A form collects structured information to act on: a lead, an application, an order. A survey measures opinion at scale. Emergent builds both, and the responses land in the same kind of database either way.

items.q: How much does an AI form builder cost?
items.a: Emergent starts free, with paid plans priced on usage rather than response counts. Typeform starts at $28 per month on annual billing for 100 responses. Jotform starts at $34 per month on annual billing for 1,000 submissions.

items.q: What is workflow automation?
items.a: Workflow automation is software that runs a sequence of steps automatically, from a trigger through decisions, data updates, and notifications, without a person doing each step by hand. It overlaps with what people call business process automation and, in the enterprise, with RPA. The difference is where the work runs and how the steps are defined. Modern workflow automation software goes further and generates the workflow, the form that fires it, and the database it writes to from a written description.

items.q: What is the difference between workflow automation and RPA?
items.a: RPA (robotic process automation) drives existing desktop and web software with a scripted user (clicks, keystrokes, form fills) to move data between systems that were never designed to talk to each other. Workflow automation talks to those systems through APIs and webhooks and reasons about the data itself. RPA suits legacy environments where the only integration point is the user interface; workflow automation suits any system with an API, which today means almost everything worth automating.

items.q: What is business process automation?
items.a: Business process automation (BPA) is the practice of automating a repeatable business process end to end, such as an invoice approval, a customer onboarding, or a support ticket lifecycle, rather than a single task inside it. Workflow automation software is what BPA is built on today. Emergent belongs in the BPA category because it generates the process, the intake form, the routing, the audit trail, and the reports as one build, not five tools stitched together.

items.q: How is Emergent different from Zapier, Make, and n8n?
items.a: Zapier, Make, and n8n are workflow engines: they run steps between apps, and anything they host, such as Zapier Tables or Interfaces, stays inside their platform. Emergent generates the workflow plus the app it triggers from, the database it writes to, and the dashboard your team reads, as one codebase you own, with no per-task meter.

items.q: What is the best workflow automation software in 2026?
items.a: It depends on what you need to own. If you want the workflow and the app around it in one codebase with no task cap, Emergent is built for that. If you want a broad catalog of pre-built integrations and are fine paying per task, Zapier has one of the largest. If you want visual canvas control at the lowest per-operation cost, Make is the value option. If you want to self-host on your own infra, n8n Community Edition is free.

items.q: Is there a free workflow automation tool?
items.a: Yes. Emergent has a free tier with monthly credits, enough to build and run a real workflow end to end. Zapier's free plan covers 100 tasks per month on two-step Zaps. Make gives 1,000 credits per month on two active scenarios. n8n's cloud plans have no free tier, but the self-hosted Community Edition is free with unlimited executions if you supply the server.

items.q: Can I connect to any tool with Emergent?
items.a: Yes. Any service with an API can be called from a workflow, whether or not Emergent has a native integration for it. No approved-partner list, no waiting on the roadmap.

items.q: Does Emergent support AI agent workflows?
items.a: Yes. Any step can be an LLM call with your prompt, your tools, and your guardrails. An agentic workflow, one where the LLM decides which tool to call next from a bounded set, is one sentence in the prompt. AI and agent steps share the same credit pool as every other step; they are not a separate meter you have to top up when the workflow gets clever.

items.q: Can I self-host the workflow?
items.a: Yes. Every workflow exports to your GitHub as real code, so you can deploy it to your own cloud, your own Kubernetes cluster, or a bare VPS. n8n's Community Edition is the other option that gives you self-hosting; Zapier and Make do not offer it at all.

items.q: What happens when I hit a task or execution limit?
items.a: You do not, because Emergent has none. On Zapier the workflow keeps running and bills the overage at up to 1.25× the base rate. On Make the scenario pauses. On n8n Cloud, workflows stop until the monthly reset or an upgrade.

items.q: Is Emergent no-code, or does it require code?
items.a: Emergent builds the workflow automation from a written description, so there is no drag-and-drop canvas to learn and no code to write for the workflow itself. When you want to change what the generated code does, such as a custom retry rule or a bespoke integration, you can drop into the code directly. It is no-code automation by default and low-code when you need it, without a plan upgrade to unlock either.

items.q: How much does workflow automation software cost?
items.a: Emergent starts free, with paid plans priced on usage rather than tasks or executions. Zapier Professional starts at $19.99/mo on annual billing for 750 tasks. Make Core starts at $9/mo on annual billing for 10,000 credits. n8n Cloud Starter is $24/mo, or $20/mo on annual billing, for 2,500 executions. On per-task tools, cost grows with every step you add, not with the value of the workflow.

items.q: Is Emergent suitable for production workflows?
items.a: Yes. Emergent is SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001 certified. Workflows can include retries, dead-letter handling, and a database-backed audit log; describe them in the prompt. For regulated workflows, contact sales about Enterprise terms before deploying.

items.q: Can Emergent build the app the workflow triggers from?
items.a: Yes. Every automation can include the intake form, the internal dashboard, and the alert channel in one build, as code you own. Zapier offers Tables and Interfaces inside its own platform; Make and n8n focus on the workflow itself.

items.q: What is a survey maker?
items.a: A survey maker is software that helps you build, publish, and collect responses from a questionnaire, whether for customer satisfaction, employee engagement, market research, event feedback, or any other structured question set. Modern survey makers do more than collect answers: they generate the questions from a description, save every response to a database you own, and push results to the tools your team already uses.

items.q: What is a quiz maker, and how is it different from a survey maker?
items.a: A survey collects opinion or measurement at scale (satisfaction, engagement, market fit); a quiz gives each respondent a personalized result (an archetype, a recommended product, a qualified lead score). Emergent is a survey maker and a quiz maker in one build, and the responses land in the same kind of database either way. If the outcome is a summary, use the survey side; if it is a per-respondent verdict, use the quiz side.

items.q: Can I build a poll with the same tool?
items.a: Yes. A poll is a survey with one or two questions and a live results view. Emergent generates the poll, the shareable link or embed, and the real-time results screen from the same prompt, and every response writes to a database with the respondent's source and any custom fields you pass. Runs alongside your surveys and quizzes on one platform, one bill.

items.q: Can I use it as a flashcard maker or a test maker for study material?
items.a: Yes. Describe the topic and the source material and Emergent generates a flashcard set, a practice test, or a full study app with scoring, timing, and progress tracking. The AI flashcard maker and test maker use the same builder as the survey and quiz side; the difference is the result screen, which shows a score card and a wrong-answer review instead of a lead capture.

items.q: What is the best free survey maker in 2026?
items.a: It depends on what you need to own. Emergent's free tier has no response cap, and custom domains are built in, using credits: the two things most free plans hold back. SurveyMonkey Basic is free but caps at 10 questions and 25 responses per survey. Typeform's free plan is 10 responses per month. Google Forms is free with no cap, but it has no custom domain, scores quizzes by points only with no personalized result screens, and keeps responses in your Google account rather than a database you own.

items.q: Which is the best AI quiz generator?
items.a: For a quiz that ships with the result screen, the lead capture, and the response database, Emergent generates the whole build from a prompt. Interact and ScoreApp use AI to help fill in a quiz template; Emergent generates the quiz, the scoring, the branching, and the app around it. If the goal is a lead-gen quiz on your own domain with responses in your CRM the same day, pick the builder that includes the app.

items.q: Does the survey, quiz, or poll have real skip logic and scoring?
items.a: Emergent includes skip logic, branching, weighted scoring, and calculations on every plan, including free. Typeform includes logic from its Basic plan; SurveyMonkey includes advanced logic from Advantage and up. Interact and ScoreApp include scoring natively, since scoring is the quiz format itself.

items.q: Can the survey, quiz, or poll capture leads?
items.a: Yes. Add an email step before or after the result and every completion becomes a row in your database with the score, the archetype, and the source attached, ready for a Slack alert, a Klaviyo flow, or a HubSpot workflow triggered by the answer.

items.q: Where do the responses live?
items.a: In a database table inside your Emergent project, which you can query, filter, and export. You can also sync each response to Google Sheets, Airtable, Notion, or your CRM in the same prompt.

items.q: Is there a response cap?
items.a: No. Emergent does not meter responses. SurveyMonkey Advantage includes 15,000 responses per year and charges $0.15 per extra. Typeform Basic stops collecting at 100 per month. Interact Lite includes 500 leads per month, and its free plan pauses quizzes at 100 completions.

items.q: Can I connect the results to my CRM?
items.a: Yes. HubSpot, Salesforce, Mailchimp, and Klaviyo are supported natively, and any other tool works through a webhook or API, with the score, archetype, and campaign attached to every result.

items.q: Can I embed the survey, quiz, or poll on my existing website?
items.a: Yes. Use an inline or iframe embed on WordPress, Webflow, Shopify, or any site. The survey, quiz, or poll also works as a standalone page on your own domain, or as a popup.

items.q: Is Emergent suitable for sensitive data like patient intake?
items.a: Emergent is SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001 certified. For regulated workflows such as HIPAA, contact sales about Enterprise terms before collecting protected health information.

items.q: How much does a survey maker, quiz maker, or poll maker cost?
items.a: Emergent starts free, with paid plans priced on usage rather than response or lead counts. SurveyMonkey Advantage is $46/mo billed annually ($552/year). Typeform Basic is $28/mo annual. Interact Lite is $27/mo annual for 500 leads. Poll Everywhere and Slido price by audience size.
